baseline_prompt_en: A layered self-portrait of the referenced woman, with the supplied image guiding her visible face and hair. Preserve her short dark bob, separated wispy fringe and natural facial proportions. She is in a narrow carousel restoration bay at blue hour, and she takes her own photograph while showing the small failure that has just been repaired. A white wooden carousel horse stands on a padded workbench behind her right shoulder. Its red carved mane panel has been returned to its place along the neck; a small brass clamp bridges the newly joined seam. Her spare right hand holds a hand-length broken wooden joining pin toward the camera, its red paint stripe and pale splintered end connecting visually to that repaired red mane. The pin is large enough to recognize as painted broken wood. Fine pale wood dust on the bench, a used sanding block and a warm test bulb beside the horse make the ongoing restoration tangible. Her face sits near the center of the frame, and her eyes meet the lens with a tired, pleased half-smile, one corner of the mouth rising as if quietly sharing the repair's ridiculous little victory. A faint dusty flush, a loose strand beside her cheek and the soft fall of an indigo linen work shirt give her an approachable everyday presence. The open shirt collar and rolled sleeves belong to the working moment. Her right elbow remains bent close to her torso; her thumb and index finger pinch the intact end of the broken pin, while her other fingers curl naturally behind it. The nearest right hand occupies the lower-right foreground, clear of her face and of the visible clamp behind her. This is the direct image from the ultra-wide camera of a smartphone held in her extended left hand, slightly above eye level and pointed back toward her. Her left shoulder, upper arm and forearm make one continuous diagonal toward the lower-left edge, where her camera-holding hand continues just beyond the frame. The short camera distance makes the near right hand and wooden pin loom larger than her centered face; the workbench and horse recede behind them. Keep the face's central proportions natural while letting the close edge hand and diverging shed lines show the broad projection. Show the scene down to her waist, with her stance supported on the workshop floor. Cool evening light enters through the open loading door behind her and warm practical light grazes the red mane, worn paint and fine grain of the broken wood. Crisp, tactile smartphone photography retains readable depth from the fingers to the clamp; the dominant connection is her expression, the broken pin and the repaired horse.
